findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a precondition that each of the three 5.5 slots has been invoked at least once and ≥15 minutes have passed (per the AWS ListMetrics docs), and record each slot's invocation evidence so that 'absent' can be told apart from 'misspelled'.

To retrieve those metrics, use GetMetricData or GetMetricStatistics."
AWS ListMetrics API reference (docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/APIReference/API_ListMetrics.html), retrieved: "After you create a metric, allow up to 15 minutes for the metric to appear."
The plan gives no precondition about invocation traffic on each of the three slots; the haiku slot (trivial reviews) may see little or no traffic right after a redeploy.

findings.finding: The plan treats a 5.5 ModelId that is missing from `list-metrics` output as evidence of a misspelled or wrong alarm dimension. It does not deal with the documented ListMetrics behaviour: a series appears only if that exact ModelId has reported data in the past two weeks, and only up to 15 minutes after the metric is first created. The only precondition stated is 'after … redeployed the production server'. Nothing requires each of the opus, sonnet and haiku slots to have been invoked at least once, ≥15 minutes before the check.
findings.location: Approach — "After the upgrade change has merged and the operator has applied the terraform and redeployed the production server, run the read-only `aws cloudwatch list-metrics` … If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series … file a bug"
scenarios: The check runs minutes after redeploy, before any trivial-class review has gone through haiku. us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5 is absent from list-metrics even though it is spelled correctly, and a bogus bug gets filed.
A slot was invoked less than 15 minutes ago. Its series hasn't propagated to ListMetrics yet, and the plan's rule reads that as 'missing'.
findings.suggested_fix: Before running list-metrics, confirm (from bot logs or a deliberate smoke invocation per slot) that opus-5-5, sonnet-5-5 and haiku-5-5 have each been invoked, then wait ≥15 minutes. In the comment, record the invocation time for each slot alongside the list-metrics output. Treat 'absent' as a finding only when the slot is known to have been invoked.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before reading list-metrics, record the redeploy/terraform-apply time and confirm each of the three 5.5 models was invoked since then. Treat an absent id as 'not yet invoked' (retry later) rather than a bug unless invocations are confirmed.

'If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series, or spelled differently, file a bug'
The AC records only the list-metrics output, the timestamp and the per-id match. It records no deploy time and no per-model invocation evidence.
findings.finding: `list-metrics` returns only series that have received data recently. A 5.5 id therefore appears only after the redeployed bot has actually invoked that model. The plan treats 'a 5.5 id is missing from the published series' as a bug signal. It neither requires nor records proof that the redeploy and terraform apply preceded the check, or that each of the three models was invoked at least once since. A missing id could be a true dimension mismatch, or just no traffic yet, for example a rarely used haiku or opus path. Conversely, the recorded AC gives no deploy or invocation evidence that the 18:06:26 PST check ran after the cutover.
findings.location: Approach ('If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series...') and the Acceptance Criteria provenance
scenarios: The check runs before any opus-5-5 request has been served. The id is absent and a spurious bug is filed.
The check runs before the redeploy completes. Only old-model series appear and the result is misread.

findings.finding: The plan runs the check only 'After the upgrade change has merged and the operator has applied the terraform and redeployed the production server', but it never checks that this state holds and gives no rule for when it doesn't. The run itself showed the state did not hold: the deployed alarms still named the 4.x ids and production still resolved 4.x. Production not redeployed: any 5.5 series seen comes from non-production callers, so the check says nothing about the production bot's own invocations.

findings.finding: The check can't tell apart 'the 5.5 id is spelled wrong in the alarm' from 'that id hasn't been called yet since the redeploy'. CloudWatch `list-metrics` only returns a ModelId series once Bedrock has recorded an invocation for it and the datapoint has been ingested. The plan runs the command right after apply/redeploy and treats any missing id as a bug to file. It doesn't require that each of the three slots (frontier/standard/trivial) has actually been called first, or that an ingestion delay has passed. The trivial slot (haiku) is the plan-review ladder's cheapest rung, so it may see little or no traffic.

findings.finding: The plan treats list-metrics output as a clean presence/absence signal, but the call only returns series that received datapoints in the recent retention window (about two weeks), and it doesn't say whose traffic produced them. So 'missing' is ambiguous: it can mean no 5.5 invocations yet, or a spelling mismatch, and both go to the same 'file a bug' branch. 'Present' can come from non-production callers, as happened in the recorded run.
findings.location: Approach — "If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series, or spelled differently, file a bug"
scenarios: The check runs right after a redeploy, before any 5.5 invocation of one class (e.g. trivial/haiku): that id is absent, and the plan files a false spelling bug.

evidence: AWS CLI list-metrics reference (awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/documentation/api/2.1.29/reference/cloudwatch/list-metrics.html), retrieved: "After you create a metric, allow up to 15 minutes before the metric appears. You can see statistics about the metric sooner by using GetMetricData or GetMetricStatistics."
infra/terraform/monitoring_eb6e.tf:75-106 — the alarm also queries InvocationClientErrors (m1-m3) by the same ModelIds; the plan's command filters only `--metric-name Invocations`.
findings.finding: The plan claims that reading the published series via list-metrics is 'the only check that observes what CloudWatch actually keys on'. AWS documentation contradicts this: GetMetricData/GetMetricStatistics return statistics for an exact dimension set sooner than ListMetrics does. Calling GetMetricData with the alarm's own six metric/dimension tuples tests exactly what the alarm will evaluate, and that includes the InvocationClientErrors series, which the plan's `--metric-name Invocations` listing never inspects.
findings.location: Approach — "Reading the published series is the only check that observes what CloudWatch actually keys on"
scenarios: Invocations is listed under the correct id, but the operator never confirms that the alarm's exact metric_query tuples resolve, so a mistake in namespace, metric name or dimension key in another query goes unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: After the list-metrics comparison, run `aws cloudwatch get-metric-data` (read-only, frontier profile, us-east-1) over the post-redeploy window with the six m1-m6 tuples copied from monitoring_eb6e.tf, and record in the ticket comment which tuples returned datapoints.
